24 A sound wave is displayed on the screen of a cathode-ray oscilloscope (c.r.o.) as shown.
1 cm
The time-base of the c.r.o. is set at 2.5 ms cm–1.
What is the frequency of the sound wave?
A
50 Hz
B
100 Hz
C
200 Hz
D
400 Hz

hints: Count the horizontal length of one complete cycle on the c.r.o. screen in cm - look from one upward zero crossing to the next upward zero crossing.
Multiply that cm length by the time-base $2.5 \text{ ms cm}^{-1}$ to get the period $T$ in ms.
Use $f = 1/T$ with $T$ converted to seconds to get the frequency in $\text{Hz}$.
walkthrough: Identify one full wave on the trace. Starting at the left edge where the trace crosses upward, the next identical upward crossing is $4.0 \text{ cm}$ to the right.
State the time-base rule: horizontal distance $\times$ time-base = time. So period $T = \text{length of one cycle} \times 2.5 \text{ ms cm}^{-1}$.
Use $f = 1/T$ to find frequency: $f = 1 / 0.010 \text{ s} = 100 \text{ Hz}$.

A.explanation: Gives half the correct frequency, from using twice the true period of $20 \text{ ms}$ instead of $10 \text{ ms}$.

B.explanation: A period of $4.0 \text{ cm}$ at $2.5 \text{ ms cm}^{-1}$ gives $T = 10 \text{ ms}$ and $f = 1/T = 100 \text{ Hz}$.

C.explanation: Gives twice the correct frequency, from using a period of only $2.0 \text{ cm}$ which is half a wave.

D.explanation: Gives four times the correct frequency, from using $1.0 \text{ cm}$ as the period instead of the full $4.0 \text{ cm}$ cycle.
